content: To maximize the benefits of this medication, it is essential to use it regularly as prescribed. Common side effects may include redness, itching, pain, or swelling at the injection site. These reactions are generally mild and temporary. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the potential benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but can occur. If you experience symptoms such as rash, severe dizziness, difficulty breathing, or swelling of the face, tongue, or throat, seek immediate medical attention. This document does not list all possible side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before using golimumab, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as natural rubber or latex, which can cause allergic reactions or other complications. Golimumab may increase your susceptibility to infections or worsen existing infections. Avoid close contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Notify your healthcare provider that you are using golimumab before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Discuss the potential risks and benefits with your doctor. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, regular laboratory and medical tests, such as complete blood counts, liver function tests, and skin examinations, should be conducted to monitor your progress and detect any potential side effects. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and lab appointments. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. Do not use it later for another condition unless directed by your doctor. Store this medication in the refrigerator and do not freeze it. Keep it in its original carton to protect it from light. If necessary, this medication may also be stored at room temperature. However, if stored at room temperature, do not return it to the refrigerator and discard it after 30 days. Discard any unused portion after use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for safe disposal methods. Your medical condition may cause complications in an emergency. Ensure that your healthcare providers are aware of your condition and the medications you are using. This information was last revised in September 2024. It is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
